route: Preconditioning the survival operator by a change of measure
headline: The decisive question (b) is answered NO, unconditionally: the least certifiable rate of the survival operator equals max over the 2^|C| profiles of rho(M_pi), a conjugation invariant, so no Doob/gauge h-transform — indeed no order-preserving change of variables — can change it; it is 1-2^{-Theta(N)} already on the player-free G_m of thm:vi-lower. The escape class is thereby characterised intrinsically as {1-Lambda >= 1/poly}. Changing the OPERATOR rather than the coordinates does move the rate: eliminating the average part (Meyer's stochastic complement) and row-normalising (Jacobi) gives a monotone operator with the same fixed point and a provably smaller rate Lambdahat <= Lambda, hence a new polynomial class strictly containing the escape class, containing every player-free game, and containing an explicit family Y_D outside all five classes of frontier.tex. It does not reach the frontier: WD(2j,j,j+4) has Lambdahat = 1-2^{1-j} exactly and the new algorithm's round count there is 4,8,17,35,70,140 — the very numbers of prop:wedge.

results.name: lem:prec-dictionary
results.statement: For every positive h on V and every positional pair, the h-transform of the killed chain is D_h^{-1} M D_h and val^h = h(t1) val / h on V'. Consequently: (b) M^h is similar to M, so G^h is stopping iff G is and every profile spectral radius is unchanged; (c) the threshold decision is preserved with the computable threshold theta h(v0)/h(t1), and the comparison predicate val(p) >= val(q) is preserved verbatim iff h(p)=h(q) and is recoverable from val^h for every h; (d) G^h is again an SSG (fair coins) iff h is constant on each connected component of the graph joining every average vertex to its two successors.
results.argument: Path weights telescope: P^h(gamma) = P(gamma) h(end)/h(start); equivalently (I-M^h)^{-1} r^h = h(t1) D_h^{-1}(I-M)^{-1} r. Dividing coordinatewise by a positive h preserves the order, so the identity survives max over sigma and min over tau. Stoppingness by lem:trapchar plus similarity. (d) is the computation h(v^(i))/(2h(v)) = 1/2.
results.verification: Exact rational check on 200 random stopping SSGs (n in 3..8, |C| <= 5) with random positive rational gauges including random h(t0), h(t1): for every one of the 2^{|C|} profiles the transformed absorption vector equalled h(t1) val / h exactly, and rho_lt(M,lam) == rho_lt(M^h,lam) at lam in {1/2,3/4,7/8}. Code: t_more.py doob_check.

results.name: thm:prec-invariance
results.statement: For every gauge h > 0 on V', (S^h)^k = D_h^{-1} S^k D_h, so the set of achievable certificate rates {lambda : exists x>0, S^h x <= lambda x} is independent of h, and lambda*(G) = inf{lambda : exists x >= 1, Sx <= lambda x} is a gauge invariant. Moreover the quantity the algorithm of thm:escape-class actually consumes, ||S^k 1||_inf, is defined without reference to h and satisfies ||S^k 1||_inf <= lambda^k kappa(x) for every certificate, so no gauge can produce a bound below it.
results.argument: S is monotone and positively homogeneous, so D_h^{-1} S D_h composes with itself; S^h x <= lambda x with x>0 iff S(D_h x) <= lambda D_h x with D_h x > 0. The last clause is monotonicity plus homogeneity applied to 1 <= x/min x.
results.verification: Structural (one line), and consistent with the exact spectral-invariance check of lem:prec-dictionary above.

results.name: lem:prec-monomial
results.statement: An invertible real A with A >= 0 and A^{-1} >= 0 is a permutation times a positive diagonal. Hence any LINEAR change of variable that is monotone with monotone inverse is a gauge up to relabelling, and by thm:prec-invariance leaves the rate unchanged; and any coordinatewise (separable) monotone change of variable differentiable at val with nonzero derivatives linearises to a positive diagonal conjugation of M_{pi*}, so the local convergence rate of value iteration is unchanged.
results.argument: With B = A^{-1} >= 0, for i != j the sum_k A_ik B_kj = 0 has nonnegative terms, so each vanishes; picking k(i) with A_{i,k(i)}B_{k(i),i} > 0 forces row k(i) of B to be supported on column i alone, and invertibility makes i -> k(i) a permutation. The separable clause is the chain rule.
results.verification: Classical (cone automorphisms of the nonnegative orthant); proof included and self-contained.

results.name: thm:prec-rate
results.statement: For any rectangular family {M_pi} of nonnegative matrices with Sx = max_pi M_pi x (the survival operator being the case of an SSG), put Lambda := max_pi rho(M_pi). Then (i) every escape certificate has lambda >= Lambda; (ii) for every rational lambda > Lambda a certificate exists and is produced by policy iteration in at most |Pi| exact linear solves, namely x = (I - M_{pi*}/lambda)^{-1} 1; (iii) lambda* = Lambda = lim ||S^k 1||^{1/k}, and for an SSG, G is stopping iff Lambda(G) < 1.
results.argument: (i) Collatz-Wielandt: M_pi x <= Sx <= lambda x with x > 0 gives rho(M_pi) <= lambda. (ii) Each A_pi = M_pi/lambda has rho < 1, so (I-A_pi)^{-1} = sum A_pi^k exists and is >= I; greedy improvement gives 1 + A_{pi'} x >= x, and iterating the monotone map y -> 1 + A_{pi'} y with A^k -> 0 gives x' >= x with strict increase at any switched coordinate, so no profile recurs and the run halts at a pi that is its own greedy successor, where Sx = lambda(x-1) <= lambda x. (iii) combines (i),(ii) with Fekete on the submultiplicative ||S^k 1||; the stopping clause is lem:trapchar (a closed class of a profile chain inside V' is a nonempty trap).
results.verification: Exact rational: on 600 random stopping SSGs across two seeds (3 <= N <= 12, |C| <= 6) and six random rational lambda each, the policy iteration returned a certificate exactly when the brute-force test rho(M_pi) < lambda over all 2^{|C|} profiles succeeded — no discrepancy. rho(M) < lambda is decided exactly by the M-matrix criterion (all leading principal minors of I - M/lambda positive). Re-run on a fresh seed with 6 <= n <= 14, 1 <= |C| <= 8, 250 games: no discrepancy. Code: prec.py escape_certificate / max_rho_profiles, t_basic.py, t_final.py.

results.name: cor:prec-characterisation
results.statement: A family of stopping SSGs carries escape certificates with log(1/lambda) >= 1/poly(N) and log kappa = poly(N) if and only if 1 - Lambda(G) >= 1/poly(N). The escape class of thm:escape-class is therefore exactly {G : 1-Lambda(G) >= 1/poly}, an intrinsic spectral condition, invariant under every gauge and every monotone linear change of variable.
results.argument: Forward is thm:prec-rate(i). Backward: if Lambda <= 1-1/p take lambda := 1-1/(3p), so Lambda <= lambda^2 and rho(A_pi) <= lambda < 1; the policy-iteration certificate x = (I-A_pi)^{-1}1 has kappa(x) <= ||x||_inf, and Cramer plus |det(I-A_pi)| >= (1-lambda)^n plus Hadamard on the cofactors gives log2 kappa = O(n log n + n log(1/(1-lambda))), polynomial.
results.verification: Exact: for G_m (m=3..9), WD(e,2,6) (e=2..8), Y_D and Z_D (D=3..8) the certificate at lambda = 1-(1-Lambda)/3 has log2 kappa = 3.5..10.2, growing linearly in N — polynomial, never the obstruction. Code: t_kappa.py.

results.name: prop:prec-Gm
results.statement: Lambda(G_m) = 1/(2u) where u is the unique root in (1/2,1) of sum_{k=1}^{m-1} u^k = 1, equivalently of 2u-1 = u^m; hence 1-Lambda(G_m) = 2^{-m}(1+o(1)). Lambda(WD(e,j,m)) = 1/(2u) where u is the unique root in (1/2,1) of sum_{k=1}^{e} u^k = 1/(2u), equivalently of (2u-1)(u+1) = 2u^{e+2}; hence 1-Lambda = (1/3)2^{-e}(1+o(1)). In both cases log(1/Lambda) = 2^{-Theta(N)}, so by thm:prec-invariance no gauge brings either into the escape class — and G_m has no players at all.
results.argument: Direct solution of the eigenvector recursion in each case (the eigenvector vanishes past the branch point in G_m; H contributes 0 in WD), giving a geometric-sum equation in u = 1/(2rho); uniqueness by monotonicity; the asymptotics by writing u = 1/2 + eps and solving 2eps = u^m, resp. eps = u^{e+2}/(u+1). On WD the a-branch profile is the survival-maximising one because the b-branch is absorbed at w_1 with probability 2^{1-j} per traversal.
results.verification: Exact bisection of the certificate programme against the closed forms agrees to twelve decimal places for m=3..9 and e=2..8; exact bisection of the two equations to m=24, e=20 confirms the constants 1 and 1/3 (ratios 1.0000 and 0.3333). This sharpens rem:escape-class, whose bound 1-lambda < 2^{1-e}/3 is exactly twice the truth. Also confirms the paper's parenthetical that the least admissible rate on Z_D is 2^{-1/2}: measured Lambda(Z_D) = 0.70710678 for D=3..8. Code: t_more.py closed_forms, t_asym.py, t_fam.py.

results.name: rem:prec-candidates
results.statement: After gauging by h the rate certified by the trivial certificate y = 1 is lambda_1(h) = max_v (Sh)(v)/h(v), and min over h of lambda_1(h) = lambda* = Lambda: the search for a preconditioner IS the certificate LP. In particular h = val (or val_sigma, or val_{sigma,tau}) has lambda_1 >= 1 on every game with a controlled vertex, with equality at a Max vertex — the value function is the worst possible gauge, because the Doob transform by a harmonic h vanishing at t0 is the chain conditioned to reach t1, which never dies. h = maximal expected survival time (the least solution of h = 1 + Sh) gives exactly lambda_1 = 1 - 1/||h||_inf.
results.argument: (S val)(v) = max_i val(v^(i)) equals val(v) at a Max vertex and is >= val(v) at a Min vertex; at an average vertex the ratio is <= 1 with equality iff no sink successor. The identity min_h lambda_1(h) = Lambda is thm:prec-rate. For the survival-time gauge Sh = h - 1 by construction.
results.verification: Exact table for G_3,5,7; H_3,5,7; S_1,3,5; WD(e,2,6) e=2,4,6; WD(2j,j,j+4) j=2,3,4; Z_D and Y_D D=3,5,7: h=1 gives 1, h=P(hit C before a sink) gives 1, h=val gives 1, h=survival time gives e.g. 0.968719 against Lambda < 0.963781 on G_5, and h = x_lambda gives essentially Lambda. Code: t_cand.py.

results.name: thm:prec-contract
results.statement: Let G be stopping with C non-empty, R(v,i;.) the first-passage law on C u {t0,t1} of the chain started at v^(i) and run through the average part, alpha_{v,i} = R(v,i;v) < 1, and That the row-normalised operator (That y)(v) = max_i g_{v,i}(y)/(1-alpha_{v,i}) at Max, min at Min, with g_{v,i}(y) = sum_{u != v} R(v,i;u) y(u) + R(v,i;t1). Then That is monotone, That(val|_C) = val|_C, |That y - That z| <= Shat |y-z|, and rho(Rhat_pi) <= rho(R_pi) <= rho(M_pi) for every profile, so Lambdahat(G) <= Lambda(G) < 1. Two-sided iteration of That brackets val|_C and val off C is the harmonic extension.
results.argument: The fixed point: by lem:transport-dim val restricted to the average part is the harmonic extension of val|_C, and a harmonic extension is the expectation of its boundary data at the exit time, so val(v^(i)) = alpha_{v,i} val(v) + g_{v,i}(val|_C); T val = val then gives t = max_i(alpha_i t + g_i), and for alpha_i < 1 that is equivalent to t = max_i g_i/(1-alpha_i) (and dually for min) — the row normalisation commutes with BOTH max and min, which is why it is legal on a game. rho(R) <= rho(M): R^k 1 counts k further visits to C, which needs k steps of survival, so R^k 1 <= M^k 1; Gelfand. rho(Rhat) <= rho(R): at the Perron vector, (Rhat x)(v) = ((rho-alpha_v)/(1-alpha_v)) x(v) <= rho x(v) since rho <= 1; reducible case by perturbation. alpha_{v,i} < 1 because otherwise {v} together with the average vertices reachable from v^(i) is a nonempty trap.
results.verification: Exact rational on 850 random stopping SSGs (three seeds; the fresh run had 6 <= n <= 14 and 1 <= |C| <= 8): T_hnf and That both fix w*|_C exactly, the harmonic extension of w*|_C reproduces w* exactly, and rho_lt(M,lam) => rho_lt(R,lam) => rho_lt(J,lam) at four random rational lam per game and every profile — no violation. Code: prec.py normal_form/T_hat/jacobi_matrix, t_basic.py, t_final.py.

results.name: thm:prec-contract-class
results.statement: There is an algorithm which computes the harmonic normal form, iterates That two-sidedly in binary fixed point with the upper iterate rounded up and the lower rounded down to multiples of 2^{-p}, p = Theta(a + log(1/(1-Lambdahat))), stops when the width falls below 4^{-a}, recovers val|_C from the midpoint by continued fractions with denominator bound 2^a and extends harmonically. It always returns val, and it halts after O((a + log kappahat)/log(1/lambdahat)) rounds. Hence SSG-Value is in P on every family with 1-Lambdahat(G) >= 1/poly(N), and that class contains the escape class of thm:escape-class (as Lambdahat <= Lambda) and every player-free game (C empty: one exact linear solve).
results.argument: Directed rounding preserves the bracket because That is monotone and fixes val|_C, and caps the bit size; the width obeys w_{k+1} <= Shat w_k + 2^{1-p}, so with a certificate it is below lambdahat^k kappahat + 2^{1-p} kappahat/(1-lambdahat); two distinct coordinates of val differ by at least 4^{-a} (lem:denominator-sharp), and |z-val| < (1/2)4^{-a} <= 1/(2q^2) makes val a continued-fraction convergent of the midpoint. Certificates for Shat at every rate above Lambdahat with polynomial conditioning by thm:prec-rate and the proof of cor:prec-characterisation, which use only nonnegativity, row sums <= 1 and rho < 1.
results.verification: Implemented end to end with exact rationals and 2^{-p} directed rounding, and checked against brute-force w*: 500 random stopping games over two seeds (plus 250 in the fresh larger re-run) returned val exactly; on the engineered families it returned val exactly for Y_D (D=3..8), Z_D (D=3..8), G_m (m=3..8, zero rounds), WD(e,2,6) (e=2..7, 4 rounds each) and WD(2j,j,j+4) (j=2..7). Code: t_algo.py, t_final.py.

results.name: prop:prec-YD
results.statement: Let Y_D be Z_D of prop:escape-family with the t0 branch of M_D replaced by a return chain of D average vertices (M_D -> (s_{D-1}, A_1), A_q -> (M_D, A_{q+1}), A_D -> (M_D, t0)). Then N = 3D+2, a = 2D, |Vmax| = D-1, |Vmin| = 1, Y_D is stopping and has the values of Z_D; 1-Lambda(Y_D) = Theta(2^{-D}) = 2^{-Theta(N)} so Y_D is outside the escape class and no gauge puts it inside; Lambdahat(Y_D) = 1/2 for every D so it is inside the contracted class, decided in 4D+1 rounds; and it lies outside all four combinatorial classes by the argument of prop:escape-family (single SCC on all 3D non-sinks carrying all three colours, a = 2D, one Max-reachability component of size D-1, |Vmax| = D-1, d(Y_D) >= d(Z_D) = D).
results.argument: The A-branch is worth (1-2^{-D}) val(M_D) < val(M_D), so the values of Z_D solve the equations of Y_D and are unique by thm:contraction. The profile choosing A_1 at M_D has the chain of prop:prec-Gm(b) with e = D. Under that action the first passage from M_D returns to M_D with probability 1-2^{-D} and dies otherwise, so its Rhat row is zero and the remaining rows are those of Z_D. For d: the optimal strategy is unique and the A-vertices have strictly larger descent level than M_D, so they lie on no descent path from a Z_D vertex.
results.verification: Exact: stopping by the trap test; values equal to Z_D's (val(s_D) = 1/(2^D-1)) for D=3..7; 1-Lambda in (5.03e-2, 2.33e-2, 1.11e-2, 5.40e-3, 2.66e-3) for D=3..7, halving with D; Lambdahat bracketed as [0.5,0.5+2^{-30}) for every D; SCC computation gives one component of size 3D carrying all three colours; Max-reachability one component of size D-1; contracted algorithm returns val in 13,17,21,25,29,33 rounds for D=3..8. Code: fams.py YD, t_sep.py, t_algo.py.

results.name: prop:prec-wedge
results.statement: For WD(e,j,m), Rhat(v_i,a;.) = 0 and Rhat(v_i,b;v_{3-i}) = 1-2^{1-j}, so Lambdahat(WD(e,j,m)) = 1-2^{1-j} exactly, independent of e and m. Hence WD(2j,j,j+4) (N = 6j+9) is outside the contracted class, while WD(e,2,m) with e growing is inside it and outside the escape class. The algorithm of thm:prec-contract-class halts on WD(2j,j,j+4) after 4, 8, 17, 35, 70, 140 rounds for j = 2..7 — the numbers of prop:wedge — and after 4 rounds on WD(e,2,6) for every e.
results.argument: The a-branch passage returns to v_i with probability 1-2^{-e} and otherwise reaches H, hence a sink: the row normalisation annihilates it. The b-branch returns to v_i with probability 1/2 and otherwise enters c_{i,1}, from which v_{3-i} is reached with probability 1-2^{1-j}; dividing by 1/2 gives 1-2^{1-j}. Rhat_pi is then 0, or has one nonzero row, or is antidiagonal with both entries 1-2^{1-j}.
results.verification: Exact bracketing of Lambdahat gives 0.5, 0.75, 0.875, 0.9375, 0.96875, 0.984375 for j=2..7, i.e. 1-2^{1-j} exactly; round counts measured with the exact end-to-end algorithm. Code: t_fam.py, t_wdj.py.

results.name: prop:prec-block
results.statement: Aggregating C into blocks and solving each block exactly (block Jacobi) keeps val as a fixed point, is monotone, costs 2^{|B|} exact linear solves per block, and has rate Lambda_B = max_pi rho(Sigma_pi) with Sigma_pi the first-passage law from a block to the other blocks; blocks of size 1 recover def:prec-contract. But the gain is at most linear in the block size: on LC(k,e) (a cycle of k Max vertices each reaching the next through a damping chain with escape 2^{-e}, N = ke+k+3) every partition with at least two blocks has Lambda_B = q^{k/r'} with q = 1-2^{-e} and r' the number of boundary crossings around the cycle, so blocks of size at most b give 1 - Lambda_B <= 1 - q^b < b 2^{-e}. With e = k = Theta(sqrt N) this is 2^{-Theta(sqrt N)} for every polynomial b: no aggregation with polynomially solvable blocks has a polynomial rate on LC.
results.argument: Theta_B(val off B) = val on B because val|_B is a fixed point of the restricted operator, which is a stopping game with terminal payoffs and so has a unique one (lem:gen-comparison, thm:contraction); the y-part of the block value is (I-R[B,B])^{-1}R[B,C\B]. On LC the survival-maximising profile takes the chain branch everywhere; a nonzero entry of Sigma_pi is a cycle segment crossing exactly one boundary, so the digraph's unique simple cycle has length r' and weight q^k and the characteristic polynomial is lambda^{|C|} - q^k lambda^{|C|-r'}. Non-crossings number at most k - |B-count|, so r' >= k/b; Bernoulli gives 1-q^b <= b 2^{-e}.
results.verification: Exact rational on all 281 partitions with at least two blocks of LC(4,3), LC(5,3), LC(4,5), LC(6,3): Lambda_B = q^{k/r'} with zero mismatches, and the optimum 1-q^b is attained by consecutive blocks whenever b divides k. Measured 1-rate on LC(k,6) for b = 1,2,4: 0.015625, 0.031006, 0.061050, i.e. 1-(63/64)^b exactly. Code: t_more.py block_matrix/blocks_on_LC, t_block.py.

results.name: prop:prec-onectrl
results.statement: If there is a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a stopping SSG and a designated controlled vertex v, outputs a stochastic game on V \ {v} whose values agree with val off v, then SSG-Value is in P. Hence aggregation is free and exact exactly on the uncontrolled (average) part, and target-equivalent as soon as it eliminates one controlled vertex.
results.argument: A controlled vertex of a stopping game has no self-loop (a self-loop is a trap), so val(v) = max_i val(v^(i)) at Max and min at Min: the eliminated game's values name an optimal successor at v. That is a sound non-stalling decision rule, and thm:decide-one-bit applies.
results.verification: Reduction to thm:decide-one-bit, whose retyping construction is exactly what is needed; no computation required.

results.name: thm:prec-target
results.statement: SSG-Value is in P if and only if there is a polynomial-time algorithm which, given a stopping SSG, outputs a monotone map F on [0,1]^{V'}, evaluable in polynomial time, with F(val) = val and ||F^k(1) - F^k(0)||_inf <= (1-1/poly(N))^k. So the unrestricted preconditioning question of part (b) is target-equivalent, and only restricted classes of preconditioner (gauges: refuted; average-part contraction: proved to help; block aggregation: proved to help only by its block size) carry unconditional content.
results.argument: Forward: take F the constant map val. Backward: monotonicity and F(val) = val give F^k(0) <= val <= F^k(1); the width falls below 4^{-a} in O(poly) steps; round outward to keep bit sizes bounded and recover val by continued fractions as in thm:prec-contract-class.
results.verification: Structural; the recovery step is the one implemented and tested end to end in t_algo.py.

results.name: measurement: the true bracket rate, and Y_D is not a stall
results.statement: The observed per-round factor of the true two-sided bracket ||T^k 1 - T^k 0||_inf at k = 120 equals Lambda to nine decimal places on G_5, G_7, WD(4,2,6), WD(7,2,6) (0.963780988, 0.991791422, 0.976750819, 0.997342154), is slightly below it on Y_D (0.985530 against 0.988904 at D=5), and is exactly 1/2 on Z_D against Lambda = 2^{-1/2}. Separately, Y_D is NOT a stall: the own-successor test of rem:own-successor for def:slack, Z-seeded and read in both directions, fires on Y_D at rounds 8, 11, 14, 17, 20 for D = 3..7 (linear), and on Z_D at round 2.
results.argument: Two consequences. First, the escape certificate is optimal among certificates (thm:prec-rate) yet still not tight for value iteration, because a tighter certificate would have to read Min as a minimiser, which lem:survival(a) cannot afford. Second, a long survival time is not by itself a difficulty: G_m has no players at all, 1-Lambda = 2^{-Theta(N)}, and is solved by one linear solve; so the fourth clause of rem:escape-class does not transfer to the contracted class either way, and whether that class contains a stall is undetermined.
results.verification: Exact rational iteration of T for 120 rounds; exact slack calculus with the free Z_0/Z_1 seed and soundness checked against brute-force w* at every round. Code: t_more.py brackets, t_stall.py.

gap: It is not determined here whether the contracted class {G : 1 - Lambdahat(G) >= 1/poly(N)} of thm:prec-contract-class contains a stopping SSG on which the own-successor test of rem:own-successor for def:slack, seeded with the free Z_0/Z_1 bounds and read in both directions, stays silent at some controlled vertex for superpolynomially many rounds — equivalently, whether the fourth clause of rem:escape-class (no member of the escape class is a stall) has any analogue for the contracted class; Y_D is not such an instance, firing at round 3D-1, and the argument of rem:escape-class does not transfer because thm:slack-vi-upper bounds Delta by the bracket of the ORIGINAL value iteration, whose rate is Lambda and not Lambdahat.
next_steps: 1. Integrate the section as it stands: it retires the change-of-measure idea unconditionally (thm:prec-invariance + thm:prec-rate + prop:prec-Gm), gives frontier.tex an intrinsic characterisation of its own escape class (cor:prec-characterisation), sharpens rem:escape-class's wedge estimate by the exact constant 1/3, and confirms its parenthetical that Lambda(Z_D) = 2^{-1/2}. 2. The one live question this route opens is the GAP above: hunt for a stall inside the contracted class. The design constraint is now explicit and narrow — such a family needs cycles among controlled vertices whose contracted escape is 1/poly (so it is not the wedge's j-direction) yet whose value gaps are 2^{-Theta(N)} and whose difference propagation is slow; note that the two known slow mechanisms are incompatible in the contracted picture, since WD's silence rate 1 - 2^{1-j} IS its contracted rate, which is why the contracted algorithm's round count on WD(2j,j,j+4) reproduces prop:wedge's 4, 8, 17, 35, 70, 140 exactly. That coincidence deserves a proof: conjecture that on any family the first firing round of the Z-seeded own-successor test and the halting round of the contracted algorithm agree up to a constant factor, which if true makes the contracted rate a NEW and computable predictor of hybrid silence and hence a design tool for the next wedge. 3. Add Y_D to the paper's stable of separating families (it is to the contracted class what Z_D is to the four combinatorial ones) and LC(k,e) as the aggregation obstruction. 4. Do NOT spend further rounds on gauges, Perron vectors, Collatz-Wielandt refinements of the survival operator, or multigrid/aggregation of the controlled part: prop:prec-block prices aggregation exactly (a factor b for a cost 2^b) and prop:prec-onectrl shows the next step past it is thm:decide-one-bit. 5. Attribution to carry into the paper: the stochastic complement is Meyer's, the row normalisation is Jacobi preconditioning, the comparison rho(J) <= rho(M) is standard for the Jacobi splitting of a nonnegative matrix; what is specific is that the normalisation commutes with both max and min, so it is legal on a game.

\section{Preconditioning the survival operator}\label{sec:precondition}

\Cref{thm:escape-class} makes the running time of two-sided value iteration
depend on a certified rate $\lambda$ for the survival operator $S$ of
\Cref{def:survival}, and \Cref{rem:escape-class} records that on the wedge
every admissible $\lambda$ has $\log_2(1/\lambda)=2^{-\Theta(N)}$. This
section asks whether a change of measure can improve that rate rather than
narrow the class. The answer has two halves. Every diagonal change of
measure --- the Doob $h$-transform, in every form in which it preserves the
decision --- leaves the rate exactly where it was, because the rate is a
spectral invariant of a conjugation
(\Cref{thm:prec-invariance,thm:prec-rate}); and the escape class is exactly
the class on which that invariant is polynomially bounded
(\Cref{cor:prec-characterisation}). A change of \emph{operator} rather than
of coordinates does move the rate: eliminating the average part and then
normalising each row gives a strictly larger polynomial class
(\Cref{thm:prec-contract-class}), which contains $G_m$, on which value
iteration is exponential by \Cref{thm:vi-lower}, and a family outside all
five polynomial classes of \Cref{sec:special} (\Cref{prop:prec-YD}); but the wedge
defeats it at exactly the rate at which it defeats the hybrid
(\Cref{prop:prec-wedge}), aggregation into blocks of size $b$ buys a factor
$b$ for a cost $2^{b}$ (\Cref{prop:prec-block}), and in full generality the
question is target-equivalent (\Cref{thm:prec-target}).

\subsection{Gauges and what they preserve}

Throughout $V'=V\setminus\{t_0,t_1\}$, and for a positional pair
$(\sigma,\tau)$ we write $M_{\sigma\tau}$ for the \emph{killed} transition
matrix on $V'$: the row of a controlled $v$ is the indicator of its chosen
successor if that lies in $V'$ and is zero otherwise, the row of an average
$v$ carries $\tfrac12$ on each successor lying in $V'$ (accumulated, so a
repeated successor carries $1$). Since $S$ maximises at \emph{every}
controlled vertex, its profiles range over all choices at $C=\Vmax\cup\Vmin$:
writing $\Pi$ for that set of $2^{|C|}$ profiles,
\[
  Sx=\max_{\pi\in\Pi}M_\pi x \qquad\text{coordinatewise on } V' .
\]

\begin{definition}[Gauge, $h$-transform]\label{def:prec-gauge}
A \emph{gauge} is a vector $h\in(0,\infty)^{V}$; $D_h$ is the diagonal matrix
it defines. The \emph{gauge transform} of the survival operator is
$S^h:=D_h^{-1}\circ S\circ D_h$ on $\mathbb R^{V'}$, and the
\emph{$h$-transform} of the game is the family of kernels
$P^h_{\sigma\tau}(u,v):=P_{\sigma\tau}(u,v)h(v)/h(u)$ on $V$, one for each
positional pair, with the sinks absorbing. Its killed part is
$M^h_{\sigma\tau}=D_h^{-1}M_{\sigma\tau}D_h$ on $V'$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[What an $h$-transform does]\label{lem:prec-dictionary}
Let $G$ be an SSG and $h\in(0,\infty)^{V}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item For every positional pair, $\val^h_{\sigma\tau}
      =h(t_1)\,\val_{\sigma\tau}/h$ on $V'$, where $\val^h_{\sigma\tau}$ is
      the $t_1$-absorption functional
      $(I-M^h_{\sigma\tau})^{-1}r^h_{\sigma\tau}$ of the transformed
      kernel; and $\val^h:=\max_\sigma\min_\tau\val^h_{\sigma\tau}$,
      $\val^{h}_\sigma:=\min_\tau\val^h_{\sigma\tau}$ obey the same
      identity, since dividing coordinatewise by a positive $h$ preserves
      the order and therefore commutes with $\max$ and $\min$.
\item $M^h_{\sigma\tau}$ is similar to $M_{\sigma\tau}$; hence $G^h$ is
      stopping if and only if $G$ is, and every spectral invariant of every
      profile chain is unchanged.
\item The threshold decision is preserved with a computable threshold:
      $\val(v_0)\ge\theta$ iff $\val^h(v_0)\ge\theta\,h(v_0)/h(t_1)$. The
      comparison predicate $\val(p)\ge\val(q)$ is preserved verbatim if and
      only if $h(p)=h(q)$, and is recoverable from $\val^h$ for every $h$.
\item $G^h$ is again an SSG --- every average vertex a fair coin --- if and
      only if $h$ is constant on each connected component of the graph on
      $V$ whose edges join every average vertex to each of its two
      successors. In particular, on any component containing an average
      vertex with a sink successor, $h$ is pinned to the value it takes at
      that sink.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) For a path $\gamma=u_0\to\cdots\to u_r$ the transformed weight
telescopes: $P^h(\gamma)=P(\gamma)h(u_r)/h(u_0)$. Summing over paths from
$u$ to $t_1$ that stay in $V'$ before their last step gives
$\val^h(u)=h(t_1)\val(u)/h(u)$; the sum converges because the transformed
Neumann series is $D_h^{-1}(\sum_kM^k)D_h$. Equivalently, and without
paths: $(I-M^h)^{-1}r^h=D_h^{-1}(I-M)^{-1}D_hD_h^{-1}r\,h(t_1)
=h(t_1)D_h^{-1}(I-M)^{-1}r$. For $\val$ and $\val_\sigma$ apply this to each
profile and use that $D_h^{-1}$ is monotone, so it commutes with the
$\max$ and $\min$ over profiles.

(b) Similarity is \Cref{def:prec-gauge}; $\rho(M^h_{\sigma\tau})
=\rho(M_{\sigma\tau})$, and by \Cref{lem:trapchar} $G$ is stopping iff
$\rho(M_{\sigma\tau})<1$ for every pair.

(c) Immediate from (a). For the second clause,
$\val^h(p)\ge\val^h(q)$ reads $\val(p)/h(p)\ge\val(q)/h(q)$, which agrees
with $\val(p)\ge\val(q)$ for all value vectors exactly when $h(p)=h(q)$.

(d) At an average $v$ the transformed probabilities are
$h(v^{(i)})/(2h(v))$, and these are $\tfrac12$ for both $i$ exactly when
$h(v^{(0)})=h(v^{(1)})=h(v)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:prec-format}
(d) is the reason the interesting reading of this section allows chance
vertices with arbitrary rational probabilities: inside the strict SSG format
a Doob transform is almost always constant, and \Cref{lem:gadget} says
nothing is lost by leaving the format, since any dyadic probability is
realised by a chain of average vertices. Every statement below is proved for
the general format and specialises.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The rate is a conjugation invariant}

\begin{theorem}[Gauge invariance of the rate]\label{thm:prec-invariance}
Let $h\in(0,\infty)^{V'}$ be a gauge. Then $(S^h)^k=D_h^{-1}S^kD_h$ for
every $k$, and consequently
\[
  \{\lambda>0:\ \exists\,x>0 \text{ with } S^hx\le\lambda x\}
  \;=\;\{\lambda>0:\ \exists\,x>0 \text{ with } Sx\le\lambda x\},
\]
so the least certifiable rate
$\lambda^\ast(G):=\inf\{\lambda:\exists x\ge\bbone,\ Sx\le\lambda x\}$
is unchanged by every gauge. The same holds for the quantity the algorithm
of \Cref{thm:escape-class} actually consumes: $\|S^k\bbone\|_\infty$ is
defined without reference to $h$, and every certificate obeys
$\|S^k\bbone\|_\infty\le\lambda^k\kappa(x)$, so no gauge can produce a bound
below $\|S^k\bbone\|_\infty$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$S$ is positively homogeneous, so $S(D_hx)$ is defined and
$S^h=D_h^{-1}SD_h$ composes with itself as stated. If $S^hx\le\lambda x$
with $x>0$ then $S(D_hx)\le\lambda D_hx$ and $D_hx>0$, and conversely. For
the last clause, $x\ge\bbone$ gives $\bbone\le x/\min x$, so by monotonicity
and homogeneity $S^k\bbone\le S^kx/\min x\le\lambda^kx/\min x
\le\lambda^k\kappa(x)$.
\end{proof}

The invariance is not an artefact of restricting to \emph{diagonal} changes
of variable: within linear changes of variable, diagonal is all there is.

\begin{lemma}[Order-isomorphisms are monomial]\label{lem:prec-monomial}
Let $A$ be an invertible real matrix with $A\ge0$ and $A^{-1}\ge0$. Then $A$
is a permutation matrix times a positive diagonal matrix. Consequently a
linear change of variable under which both the map and its inverse are
monotone conjugates $S$ into $D^{-1}P^{-1}SPD$ for a permutation $P$ and a
positive diagonal $D$, and \Cref{thm:prec-invariance} applies. If instead
$\Phi$ is a coordinatewise (separable) monotone change of variable,
differentiable at $\val$ with nonzero derivatives, then the linearisation of
$\Phi^{-1}\circ T\circ\Phi$ at $\Phi^{-1}(\val)$ is $D^{-1}M_{\pi}D$ for a
positive diagonal $D$ and the profile $\pi$ optimal near $\val$, so the local
convergence rate of value iteration is unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $B=A^{-1}\ge0$. For $i\ne j$, $\sum_kA_{ik}B_{kj}=0$ is a sum of
nonnegative terms, so $A_{ik}B_{kj}=0$ for every $k$. From
$\sum_kA_{ik}B_{ki}=1$ pick $k(i)$ with $A_{ik(i)}B_{k(i)i}>0$; then
$B_{k(i)j}=0$ for every $j\ne i$, so row $k(i)$ of $B$ is supported on
column $i$ alone. Since $B$ is invertible no two rows are supported on the
same column and none is zero, so $k$ is a permutation and $B$, hence $A$, is
monomial. The last clause is the chain rule: a separable $\Phi$ has diagonal
derivative.
\end{proof}

The next theorem identifies $\lambda^\ast$ and is what makes the invariance
decisive: there is nothing for a preconditioner to gain, because the
certificate programme is already tight.

\begin{theorem}[The certifiable rate is the worst profile's spectral
radius]\label{thm:prec-rate}
Let $\{M_\pi\}_{\pi\in\Pi}$ be any \emph{rectangular} family of nonnegative
$n\times n$ matrices --- at each row index a finite set of allowed rows,
$\Pi$ the product of those sets --- and $Sx:=\max_\pi M_\pi x$
coordinatewise; the survival operator of an SSG is the case in which the
rows of a controlled vertex are the two indicators of its successors and an
average vertex has the single row $\tfrac12(e_{v^{(0)}}+e_{v^{(1)}})$.
Put $\Lambda:=\max_{\pi\in\Pi}\rho(M_\pi)$. Then
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item every escape certificate $(\lambda,x)$ --- a pair with $x\ge\bbone$ and
      $Sx\le\lambda x$, as in \Cref{def:survival} --- has
      $\lambda\ge\Lambda$; hence
      $\lambda^\ast:=\inf\{\lambda:\exists x\ge\bbone,\ Sx\le\lambda x\}
      \ge\Lambda$;
\item for every rational $\lambda>\Lambda$ an escape certificate at rate
      $\lambda$ exists, and one is produced by policy iteration in at most
      $|\Pi|$ exact linear solves: with $A_\pi:=M_\pi/\lambda$, iterate
      $x_{n}:=(I-A_{\pi_n})^{-1}\bbone$ and let $\pi_{n+1}$ be greedy for
      $x_n$; the iterates increase strictly, the run terminates, and its
      last $x$ satisfies $Sx=\lambda(x-\bbone)\le\lambda x$, $x\ge\bbone$;
\item hence $\lambda^\ast=\Lambda=\lim_k\|S^k\bbone\|_\infty^{1/k}$; and for
      the survival operator of an SSG, $G$ is stopping iff $\Lambda(G)<1$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) $M_\pi x\le Sx\le\lambda x$ with $x\ge\bbone>0$, so by the
Collatz--Wielandt inequality for nonnegative matrices
$\rho(M_\pi)\le\max_v(M_\pi x)(v)/x(v)\le\lambda$.

(ii) Each $A_\pi$ is nonnegative with $\rho(A_\pi)=\rho(M_\pi)/\lambda<1$,
so $(I-A_\pi)^{-1}=\sum_kA_\pi^k$ exists, is nonnegative, and
$x_n=\sum_kA_{\pi_n}^k\bbone\ge\bbone>0$. If $\pi_{n+1}$ is greedy for
$x_n$ then $A_{\pi_{n+1}}x_n\ge A_{\pi_n}x_n$, so
$\bbone+A_{\pi_{n+1}}x_n\ge x_n$; applying the monotone map
$y\mapsto\bbone+A_{\pi_{n+1}}y$ repeatedly and using $A^k\to0$ gives
$x_{n+1}\ge x_n$, and at a coordinate where the greedy choice changed the
inequality is strict, so no profile recurs. The run therefore stops at a
$\pi$ that is its own greedy successor, where
$Sx=\lambda A_\pi x=\lambda(x-\bbone)$.

(iii) (i) and (ii) give $\lambda^\ast=\Lambda$. For the limit,
$S^{k+l}\bbone\le\|S^l\bbone\|_\infty S^k\bbone$ makes
$\|S^k\bbone\|_\infty$ submultiplicative, so the limit exists; it is at
least $\lim\|M_\pi^k\bbone\|^{1/k}=\rho(M_\pi)$ for each $\pi$ and at most
$\lambda$ for every certificate rate by
\Cref{thm:prec-invariance}. Stopping: $\rho(M_\pi)=1$ for some $\pi$ iff
some profile chain has a closed class inside $V'$, which by
\Cref{lem:trapchar} is a nonempty trap.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The escape class, intrinsically]\label{cor:prec-characterisation}
Let $\mathcal F$ be a family of stopping SSGs. Then $\mathcal F$ carries
escape certificates with $\log_2(1/\lambda)\ge1/\mathrm{poly}(N)$ and
$\log_2\kappa=\mathrm{poly}(N)$ if and only if
$1-\Lambda(G)\ge1/\mathrm{poly}(N)$ on $\mathcal F$. Membership of the class
is therefore a property of the spectral radii of the $2^{|C|}$ profile
chains, and by \Cref{thm:prec-invariance,lem:prec-monomial} it is invariant
under every gauge and every monotone linear change of variable.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
($\Rightarrow$) is \Cref{thm:prec-rate}(i). ($\Leftarrow$) Suppose
$\Lambda\le1-1/p$ with $p=p(N)$ a polynomial, and take the rational
$\lambda:=1-1/(3p)$, so $\lambda^2\ge1-2/(3p)\ge\Lambda$ and hence
$\rho(A_\pi)\le\Lambda/\lambda\le\lambda<1$ for every $\pi$. Let $x$ be the
certificate of \Cref{thm:prec-rate}(ii); then $\kappa(x)\le\|x\|_\infty$
because $x\ge\bbone$, and with $n=|V'|$, writing
$x=(I-A_{\pi})^{-1}\bbone=\mathrm{adj}(I-A_\pi)\bbone/\det(I-A_\pi)$, every
eigenvalue of $A_\pi$ has modulus at most $\lambda$, so
$|\det(I-A_\pi)|\ge(1-\lambda)^{n}$, while Hadamard's inequality bounds
every cofactor of $I-A_\pi$ by $(\sqrt n\,(1+1/\lambda))^{\,n-1}$. Hence
\[
  \log_2\kappa(x)\;\le\;n\log_2 n+n\log_2\!\bigl(1+1/\lambda\bigr)
   +n\log_2\frac1{1-\lambda}+\log_2 n,
\]
which is polynomial in $N$ since $\log_2\frac1{1-\lambda}=\log_2(3p)$. Now
$\log_2(1/\lambda)\ge1/(3p)$ and \Cref{thm:escape-class} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:prec-verified}
Every identity above was checked in exact rational arithmetic. On $600$
random stopping SSGs (two independent seeds, $3\le N\le12$, $|C|\le6$) and
six random rational $\lambda$ each, the policy iteration of
\Cref{thm:prec-rate}(ii) returned a certificate exactly when
$\rho(M_\pi)<\lambda$ for all $2^{|C|}$ profiles, tested by the M-matrix
criterion (all leading principal minors of $I-M_\pi/\lambda$ positive), with
no discrepancy; the identity of \Cref{lem:prec-dictionary}(a) and the
spectral invariance (b) were verified on $200$ random stopping games against
random positive rational gauges, every profile, exactly.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The invariant, computed}

\begin{proposition}[The rate of $G_m$ and of the wedge]\label{prop:prec-Gm}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item For the player-free family $G_m$ of \Cref{thm:vi-lower},
      $\Lambda(G_m)=1/(2u_m)$ where $u_m$ is the unique root in
      $(\tfrac12,1)$ of $\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}u^{k}=1$, equivalently of
      $2u-1=u^{m}$; consequently $1-\Lambda(G_m)=2^{-m}(1+o(1))$ and
      $\log_2(1/\Lambda(G_m))=2^{-\Theta(N)}$ with $N=2m+2$.
\item For $WD(e,j,m)$ of \Cref{def:wedge}, $\Lambda=1/(2u)$ where $u$ is the
      unique root in $(\tfrac12,1)$ of $\sum_{k=1}^{e}u^{k}=1/(2u)$,
      equivalently of $(2u-1)(u+1)=2u^{e+2}$; consequently
      $1-\Lambda=\tfrac13 2^{-e}(1+o(1))$ and
      $\log_2(1/\Lambda)=2^{-\Theta(N)}$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular no gauge, and no monotone linear change of variable, brings
either family into the escape class; and $G_m$ has \emph{no players at all}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(a) There are no controlled vertices, so $\Pi$ is a singleton and
$\Lambda=\rho(M)$. Row $c_L$ of $M$ is zero, and for $m\le i\le L-1$ the row
is $\tfrac12$ on $c_{i+1}$ alone; so a right eigenvector for
$\rho\ne0$ has $x(c_i)=0$ for $i\ge m$ by downward induction from
$x(c_L)=0$. For $i\le m-1$, $\rho x(c_i)=\tfrac12x(c_{i+1})+\tfrac12x(c_1)$.
Normalise $x(c_1)=1$ and put $u:=1/(2\rho)$; then $x(c_{m-1})=u$ and
$x(c_i)=u(1+x(c_{i+1}))$, whence $1=x(c_1)=\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}u^{k}$. The
polynomial $\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}u^k$ is strictly increasing on $(0,1)$, equals
$1-2^{-(m-1)}<1$ at $u=\tfrac12$ and $m-1\ge2$ at $u=1$, so the root is
unique and lies in $(\tfrac12,1)$; multiplying by $1-u$ turns the equation
into $2u-1=u^{m}$. Write $u=\tfrac12+\varepsilon$; then
$2\varepsilon=u^{m}>2^{-m}$, and if $\varepsilon\le1/m$ then
$2\varepsilon=2^{-m}(1+2\varepsilon)^{m}\le e^{2}2^{-m}$, which is below
$2/m$ for $m\ge5$, so the root does satisfy $\varepsilon\le1/m$ by
monotonicity. Hence $\varepsilon=2^{-m-1}(1+O(m2^{-m}))$ and
$1-\Lambda=2\varepsilon/(1+2\varepsilon)=2^{-m}(1+o(1))$.

(b) $\Vmin=\emptyset$ and $S$ maximises at $v_1,v_2$; take the profile
$\pi$ that chooses $a_{i,1}$ at both. The two halves do not communicate
under $\pi$, so $\rho(M_\pi)$ is computed on one of them. With
$x(v_1)=1$ and $u:=1/(2\rho)$: $x(H)=0$ since $H$'s successors are sinks;
$x(a_{1,e})=u$; $x(a_{1,q})=u(1+x(a_{1,q+1}))$; and
$x(a_{1,1})=\rho x(v_1)=1/(2u)$. Hence $\sum_{k=1}^{e}u^{k}=1/(2u)$.
Multiplying by $2u(1-u)$ gives $2u^{2}-2u^{e+2}=1-u$, i.e.
$(2u-1)(u+1)=2u^{e+2}$; at $u=\tfrac12$ the left side vanishes and the right
does not, at $u=1$ the left is $2$ and the right is $2$, and the difference
is strictly monotone between, so the root is unique in $(\tfrac12,1)$. It is
the largest profile radius: the remaining three profiles replace one or both
$a$-branches by $b$-branches, whose chains are absorbed at $w_1$ with
probability $2^{1-j}$ per traversal and are therefore faster. Writing
$u=\tfrac12+\varepsilon$ gives $\varepsilon=u^{e+2}/(u+1)$, so
$\varepsilon=\tfrac13 2^{-e-1}(1+o(1))$ and $1-\Lambda=2\varepsilon/(1+2\varepsilon)
=\tfrac13 2^{-e}(1+o(1))$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Changing the operator: contraction of the average part}

A gauge changes coordinates and cannot move the rate. What can move it is a
change of the \emph{operator} preserving the fixed point. The average part
of an SSG carries no choices, so it can be eliminated exactly and once and
for all; this is Meyer's stochastic complementation, prior art, and it is
the harmonic normal form of the document's item (v4).

\begin{definition}[Harmonic normal form, contracted
operator]\label{def:prec-contract}
Let $G$ be stopping, $C=\Vmax\cup\Vmin\ne\emptyset$, $A=\Vavg$. For
$v\in C$ and $i\in\{0,1\}$ let $R(v,i;\cdot)$ be the law on
$C\cup\{t_0,t_1\}$ of the first vertex of $C\cup\{t_0,t_1\}$ visited by the
chain started at $v^{(i)}$ and run through $A$, and write
$r(v,i):=R(v,i;t_1)$. Put $\alpha_{v,i}:=R(v,i;v)$ and define, on
$y\in\mathbb R^{C}$,
\[
  g_{v,i}(y):=\sum_{u\in C\setminus\{v\}}R(v,i;u)\,y(u)+r(v,i),
  \qquad
  (\widehat Ty)(v):=\begin{cases}
     \max_i g_{v,i}(y)/(1-\alpha_{v,i}), & v\in\Vmax,\\
     \min_i g_{v,i}(y)/(1-\alpha_{v,i}), & v\in\Vmin.
  \end{cases}
\]
Write $\widehat R_\pi$ for the matrix with rows
$R(v,\pi(v);\cdot)|_{C\setminus\{v\}}/(1-\alpha_{v,\pi(v)})$ and
$\widehat\Lambda(G):=\max_{\pi\in\Pi}\rho(\widehat R_\pi)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Well-posedness]\label{lem:prec-wellposed}
On a stopping $G$: the matrix $I-P_{AA}$ is invertible, so $R$ is defined
and computable by one factorisation and $2|C|$ right-hand sides; every entry
of $R$ and of $\widehat R$ is a rational of bit size $O(a+\log N)$; and
$\alpha_{v,i}<1$ for every $v,i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
A trap of the sub-chain on $A$ is a set every one of whose average vertices
has both successors in it, hence a trap of $G$, hence empty by
\Cref{lem:trapchar}; so the chain leaves $A$ almost surely and
$\rho(P_{AA})<1$. The bit size is \Cref{lem:denominator-sharp} applied to
the linear system, whose matrix is $2I-2P_{AA}$ with integer entries and row
sums at most $2$. If $\alpha_{v,i}=1$ then $U:=\{v\}\cup\{a\in A:a$ reachable
from $v^{(i)}$ inside $A\}$ is a nonempty trap: an average vertex of $U$ with
a successor outside $U\cup\{v\}$ would put positive mass off $v$ in
$R(v,i;\cdot)$, and $v$ has the successor $v^{(i)}\in U$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The contracted operator]\label{thm:prec-contract}
Let $G$ be stopping with $C\ne\emptyset$. Then
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $\widehat T$ is monotone, does not depend on $y(v)$ in its $v$-th
      coordinate, and $\widehat T(\val|_C)=\val|_C$;
\item $|\widehat Ty-\widehat Tz|\le\widehat S|y-z|$, where
      $\widehat Sw:=\max_\pi\widehat R_\pi w$;
\item $\rho(\widehat R_\pi)\le\rho(R_\pi)\le\rho(M_\pi)$ for every profile,
      so $\widehat\Lambda(G)\le\Lambda(G)<1$;
\item with $\widehat u_0=\bbone$, $\widehat l_0=0$ on $C$ and
      $\widehat u_{k+1}=\widehat T\widehat u_k$,
      $\widehat l_{k+1}=\widehat T\widehat l_k$, one has
      $\widehat l_k\le\val|_C\le\widehat u_k$ and
      $\widehat u_k-\widehat l_k\le\widehat S^{k}\bbone$; and $\val$ off $C$
      is the harmonic extension of $\val|_C$ (\Cref{lem:transport-dim}).
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) Monotonicity is clear, as is the absence of $y(v)$. For the fixed point:
by \Cref{lem:transport-dim} the restriction of $\val$ to $A$ is the harmonic
extension of $\val|_C$ with the sinks pinned, and a harmonic extension is
the expectation of its boundary data at the exit time, so for every
$v\in C$ and $i$,
\[
  \val(v^{(i)})=\sum_{u\in C}R(v,i;u)\,\val(u)+r(v,i)
   =\alpha_{v,i}\val(v)+g_{v,i}(\val|_C),
\]
whether or not $v^{(i)}$ lies in $A$. Since $T\val=\val$, at $v\in\Vmax$ this
gives $\val(v)=\max_i(\alpha_{v,i}\val(v)+g_{v,i}(\val|_C))$ and at
$v\in\Vmin$ the same with $\min$. Now for numbers $\alpha_i\in[0,1)$ and $g_i\ge0$,
\[
  t=\max_i(\alpha_it+g_i)
  \iff \bigl[\forall i:\ t(1-\alpha_i)\ge g_i\bigr]\ \wedge\
       \bigl[\exists i:\ t(1-\alpha_i)=g_i\bigr]
  \iff t=\max_i\frac{g_i}{1-\alpha_i},
\]
and dually for $\min$ (both equivalences use $\alpha_i<1$, which is
\Cref{lem:prec-wellposed}); apply this at each $v$ with $t=\val(v)$.

(ii) Each row of $\widehat R_\pi$ is nonnegative with sum at most $1$, and a
maximum (or minimum) of affine maps with such coefficient rows is
nonexpansive coordinatewise against the maximum over the rows.

(iii) For the second inequality, $(R_\pi^{k}\bbone)(v)$ is the probability
that the chain from $v$ under $\pi$ visits $C$ at least $k$ more times before
absorption, which requires surviving at least $k$ steps, so
$R_\pi^{k}\bbone\le M_\pi^{k}\bbone$; take $k$-th roots and use Gelfand's
formula, valid because $\|B^k\|_\infty=\|B^k\bbone\|_\infty$ for
$B\ge0$. For the first, let $R:=R_\pi$, $D:=\mathrm{diag}(\alpha_{v,\pi(v)})$
and $\widehat R=(I-D)^{-1}(R-D)$. If $R$ is irreducible with Perron vector
$x>0$ and $Rx=\rho x$ then
$(\widehat Rx)(v)=\frac{\rho-\alpha_v}{1-\alpha_v}x(v)\le\rho\,x(v)$, the
inequality being $\rho\alpha_v\le\alpha_v$, which holds because
$\rho\le1$; hence $\rho(\widehat R)\le\rho$. In general perturb $R$ to
$R+\varepsilon E$ with $E$ all-ones, which is irreducible and, for small
$\varepsilon$, still has spectral radius below $1$ and diagonal below $1$;
let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, the spectral radii and the entries being
continuous.

(iv) $\widehat l_0\le\val|_C\le\widehat u_0$ and $\widehat T$ is monotone
with $\widehat T\val|_C=\val|_C$, so the bracket is preserved; the width
bound is (ii) iterated.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The contracted escape class]\label{thm:prec-contract-class}
There is an algorithm which, given a stopping SSG $G$ with $C\ne\emptyset$,
computes the harmonic normal form and then iterates $\widehat T$ two-sidedly
in binary fixed point with the upper iterate rounded up and the lower
rounded down to multiples of $2^{-p}$, $p:=\Theta(a+\log_2\frac1{1-\widehat\Lambda})$,
stopping when the width falls below $4^{-a}$, and then returns the rational
vector of denominator at most $2^{a}$ nearest the midpoint, extended
harmonically. It always returns $\val$, and it stops after
\[
  O\!\left(\frac{a+\log_2\widehat\kappa}{\log_2(1/\widehat\lambda)}\right)
\]
rounds whenever $(\widehat\lambda,\widehat x)$ is an escape certificate for
$\widehat S$. Consequently \Cref{prob:main} is decidable in polynomial time
on every family with $1-\widehat\Lambda(G)\ge1/\mathrm{poly}(N)$, and that
class contains the escape class of \Cref{thm:escape-class} by
\Cref{thm:prec-contract}(iii).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Directed rounding preserves $\widehat l_k\le\val|_C\le\widehat u_k$ because
$\widehat T$ is monotone and fixes $\val|_C$; it also keeps every iterate a
multiple of $2^{-p}$, so the bit size does not grow. The width obeys
$\widehat u_{k+1}-\widehat l_{k+1}\le\widehat S(\widehat u_k-\widehat l_k)
+2^{1-p}\bbone$, whence, using the certificate,
$\|\widehat u_k-\widehat l_k\|_\infty\le\widehat\lambda^{k}\widehat\kappa
+2^{1-p}\widehat\kappa/(1-\widehat\lambda)$, which is below $4^{-a}$ for the
stated $p$ and $k$. Two distinct coordinates of $\val$ differ by at least
$4^{-a}$ by \Cref{lem:denominator-sharp}, so once the width is below
$4^{-a}$ the midpoint $z$ satisfies $|z(v)-\val(v)|<\tfrac12 4^{-a}
\le1/(2q^{2})$ for the denominator $q\le2^{a}$ of $\val(v)$, so $\val(v)$ is
the unique rational of denominator at most $2^{a}$ that close to $z(v)$ and
is recovered by continued fractions. The harmonic extension is
\Cref{lem:transport-dim}. The certificate for $\widehat S$ exists at every rate above
$\widehat\Lambda$, with $\log_2\widehat\kappa$ polynomial, by
\Cref{thm:prec-rate} and the proof of \Cref{cor:prec-characterisation}
applied to the rectangular family $\{\widehat R_\pi\}$ --- these are
nonnegative with row sums at most $1$ and spectral radius below $1$ by
\Cref{thm:prec-contract}(iii), which is all those arguments use.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:prec-attribution}
Nothing in \Cref{def:prec-contract} is new in isolation. Eliminating the
uncontrolled part is Meyer's stochastic complementation; dividing a row by
one minus its diagonal entry is the Jacobi preconditioner of numerical
linear algebra, and \Cref{thm:prec-contract}(iii) is the standard comparison
$\rho(J)\le\rho(M)$ for the Jacobi splitting of a nonnegative matrix. What
is specific here is (i) --- that the row normalisation commutes with
\emph{both} $\max$ and $\min$, so that it is a legitimate operation on a
game and not only on a chain --- and the resulting class.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[A family the contraction reaches and nothing else
does]\label{prop:prec-YD}
For $D\ge3$ let $Y_D$ be $Z_D$ of \Cref{prop:escape-family} with the $t_0$
branch of $M_D$ replaced by a return chain of $D$ average vertices:
\[
  M_D\to(s_{D-1},A_1),\qquad A_q\to(M_D,A_{q+1})\ (q<D),\qquad
  A_D\to(M_D,t_0),
\]
all $A_q$ average. Then $N=3D+2$, $a=2D$, $|\Vmax|=D-1$, $|\Vmin|=1$, $Y_D$
is stopping, $\val_{Y_D}$ agrees with $\val_{Z_D}$ on the vertices of $Z_D$
(and $\val(A_q)=(1-2^{q-D-1})\val(M_D)$), and
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $1-\Lambda(Y_D)=\Theta(2^{-D})=2^{-\Theta(N)}$, so $Y_D$ is outside the
      escape class, and by \Cref{thm:prec-invariance} no gauge puts it
      inside;
\item $\widehat\Lambda(Y_D)=\tfrac12$ for every $D$, so $Y_D$ is inside the
      contracted class and \Cref{thm:prec-contract-class} decides it in
      $O(N)$ rounds --- measured exactly as $4D+1$ rounds for
      $D=3,\dots,8$;
\item all $3D$ non-sinks lie in a single strongly connected component,
      which therefore carries all three colours, so \Cref{thm:kacyclic}
      does not apply, and neither does any refinement of it treating the
      components separately;
      $a=2D$, so \Cref{thm:few-avg} gives $2^{\Theta(N)}$; the
      Max-reachability digraph is one component of size $D-1$, so
      \Cref{thm:component-bound} gives $2^{\Theta(N)}$;
      $|\Vmax|=D-1$, so \Cref{thm:subexp} gives $e^{2\sqrt{D-1}}$; and
      $d(Y_D)\ge d(Z_D)=D$, so \Cref{thm:few-escape} gives $2^{\Theta(N)}$.
\end{enumerate}
So $Y_D$ stands to the contracted class as $Z_D$ stands to the four
combinatorial ones.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Stopping and the values: the $A$-chain reaches $M_D$ with probability
$1-2^{-D}$ from $A_1$ and $t_0$ otherwise, so
$\val(A_1)=(1-2^{-D})\val(M_D)<\val(M_D)$ unless $\val(M_D)=0$; hence
$\max(\val(s_{D-1}),\val(A_1))=\val(s_{D-1})$ is consistent, and the values
of $Z_D$ solve the equations of $Y_D$; uniqueness is
\Cref{thm:contraction}. Stopping is \Cref{lem:trapchar}: every $A_q$ is
average with $M_D$ among its successors and $M_D$ has $s_{D-1}$, whose chain
leaves.

(i) Take $\pi$ choosing $A_1$ at $M_D$ and anything elsewhere; the resulting
chain restricted to $\{M_D,A_1,\dots,A_D\}$ is the chain of
\Cref{prop:prec-Gm}(b) with $e=D$, so $\rho(M_\pi)=1/(2u)$ with
$\sum_{k=1}^{D}u^{k}=1/(2u)$ and $1-\rho=\Theta(2^{-D})$.

(ii) Under the action $A_1$ the first passage from $M_D$ returns to $M_D$
with probability $1-2^{-D}$ and is absorbed at $t_0$ otherwise, so that row
of $\widehat R$ is zero; the other rows are those of $Z_D$, whose contracted
matrix has $\rho=\tfrac12$ for every profile. (Both computed exactly.)

(iii) The cycle $s_D\to M_D\to s_{D-1}\to\cdots\to s_1\to W\to s_D$ of
\Cref{prop:escape-family} survives, and $M_D\to A_1\to M_D$ attaches the
chain to it; the counts are as stated. For $d$: the optimal strategy is
unique and chooses $s_{j-1}$ at every $M_j$ (the alternative is worth $0$ or
$(1-2^{-D})\val(M_D)$, both strictly less), the levels of
\Cref{lem:descent} of the $A$-vertices exceed that of $M_D$, so no $A$
vertex lies on a descent path from a $Z_D$ vertex, and $A_{\sigma^\ast}$
restricted to the $Z_D$ vertices is that of $Z_D$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The wedge defeats the contraction, at the same
rate]\label{prop:prec-wedge}
For $WD(e,j,m)$ of \Cref{def:wedge}, the contracted matrix is
\[
  \widehat R(v_i,a;\cdot)=0,\qquad
  \widehat R(v_i,b;v_{3-i})=1-2^{1-j},
\]
so $\widehat\Lambda(WD(e,j,m))=1-2^{1-j}$ exactly, independent of $e$ and
$m$. Hence on $WD(2j,j,j+4)$, where $N=6j+9$,
$\log_2(1/\widehat\Lambda)=2^{-\Theta(N)}$ and the family is outside the
contracted class; whereas on $WD(e,2,m)$ with $e$ growing it is inside,
while being outside the escape class by \Cref{prop:prec-Gm}(b). Measured
exactly, the algorithm of \Cref{thm:prec-contract-class} halts on
$WD(2j,j,j+4)$ after
\[
  4,\ 8,\ 17,\ 35,\ 70,\ 140 \quad\text{rounds for } j=2,\dots,7,
\]
which are the numbers of \Cref{prop:wedge}, and after $4$ rounds on
$WD(e,2,6)$ for every $e=2,\dots,7$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The passage from $v_i$ under the $a$-branch returns to $v_i$ with
probability $1-2^{-e}$ and reaches $H$, hence a sink, otherwise; the row
normalisation annihilates it. Under the $b$-branch, $b_i$ returns to $v_i$
with probability $\tfrac12$ and enters $c_{i,1}$ otherwise, from which
$v_{3-i}$ is reached with probability $1-2^{1-j}$ and $w_1$, hence a sink,
otherwise; dividing by $1-\tfrac12$ gives the stated entry. The matrix
$\widehat R_\pi$ is then either $0$, or has one nonzero row, or is
antidiagonal with both entries $1-2^{1-j}$, and only the last has nonzero
spectral radius, equal to $1-2^{1-j}$. The round counts are measurements.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Aggregation}

\begin{definition}[Block contraction]\label{def:prec-block}
Let $\mathcal B$ be a partition of $C$. For a block $B$ and $y$ on
$C\setminus B$ let $\Theta_B(y)$ be the value on $B$ of the normal-form game
restricted to $B$ in which arriving at $u\notin B$ pays $y(u)$; put
$\Theta(y):=(\Theta_B(y|_{C\setminus B}))_{B\in\mathcal B}$ and
$\Sigma_\pi:=$ the matrix whose $B$-rows are
$(I-R_{\pi}[B,B])^{-1}R_\pi[B,C\setminus B]$, the law of the first visit to
another block. Write $\Lambda_{\mathcal B}:=\max_\pi\rho(\Sigma_\pi)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Block contraction, and its price]\label{prop:prec-block}
$\Theta$ is monotone, $\Theta(\val|_C)=\val|_C$,
$|\Theta y-\Theta z|\le\max_\pi\Sigma_\pi|y-z|$, and $\Theta_B$ is
computable in $2^{|B|}$ exact linear solves; so
\Cref{thm:prec-contract-class} holds verbatim with $\widehat\Lambda$
replaced by $\Lambda_{\mathcal B}$ whenever every block has
$|B|=O(\log N)$. Blocks of size $1$ recover \Cref{def:prec-contract}. But
the gain is at most linear in the block size, and this is exact: let
$LC(k,e)$ have $\Vmax=\{v_1,\dots,v_k\}$, one average $f\to(t_1,t_0)$, and
damping chains
\[
  v_i\to(p_{i,1},f),\qquad p_{i,q}\to(v_{i+1},p_{i,q+1})\ (q<e),\qquad
  p_{i,e}\to(v_{i+1},t_0)
\]
(indices mod $k$), so that $N=ke+k+3$ and the first passage from $v_i$ under
its first action reaches $v_{i+1}$ with probability $q:=1-2^{-e}$. Then for
\emph{every} partition of $C$ with at least two blocks,
\[
  \Lambda_{\mathcal B}(LC(k,e))=q^{\,k/r'},
\]
where $r'$ is the number of indices $i$ with $v_i,v_{i+1}$ in different
blocks; hence if every block has at most $b$ vertices then $r'\ge k/b$ and
\[
  1-\Lambda_{\mathcal B}\;\le\;1-q^{\,b}\;<\;b\,2^{-e},
\]
attained by any partition into $k/b$ consecutive blocks. With
$e=k=\Theta(\sqrt N)$ this is $2^{-\Theta(\sqrt N)}$ for every
$b=\mathrm{poly}(N)$, so no aggregation whose blocks can be solved in
polynomial time has a polynomial rate on $LC$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$\Theta_B(\val|_{C\setminus B})=\val|_B$ because $\val|_B$ is a fixed point
of the restricted operator, which is the operator of a stopping game with
terminal payoffs $y$ and therefore has a unique one
(\Cref{lem:gen-comparison,thm:contraction}); monotonicity in $y$ is
\Cref{lem:gen-comparison}; and for a fixed profile the block value is
$(I-R[B,B])^{-1}(R[B,C\setminus B]y+r)$, whose $y$-part is $\Sigma_\pi$.

For $LC$: the profile maximising survival takes the chain branch at every
$v_i$ (the alternative $f$ is absorbed at once), and then $R(v_i;v_{i+1})=q$
is the only nonzero entry. A nonzero entry $\Sigma_\pi(v,u)$ records a segment of the $k$-cycle from
$v$ to $u$ crossing exactly one block boundary, at its last step; so a
closed walk in the digraph of $\Sigma_\pi$ projects to a closed walk in the
$k$-cycle, the unique simple cycle of that digraph has length $r'$ and
weight $q^{k}$, and the characteristic polynomial is
$\lambda^{|C|}-q^{k}\lambda^{|C|-r'}$, so $\rho=q^{k/r'}$. The number of non-crossings is at most
$\sum_B(|B|-1)=k-|\mathcal B|$, and with blocks of size at most $b$ it is at
most $k-k/b$, so $r'\ge k/b$; $1-q^{b}\le b(1-q)=b2^{-e}$ by Bernoulli.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:prec-block-verified}
The identity $\Lambda_{\mathcal B}=q^{k/r'}$ was verified in exact rational
arithmetic on all $281$ partitions with at least two blocks of $LC(4,3)$,
$LC(5,3)$, $LC(4,5)$ and $LC(6,3)$, with no discrepancy, and the optimum
$1-q^{b}$ was attained exactly by consecutive blocks whenever $b$ divides
$k$. As with $Z_D$ and $Y_D$, $LC$ defeats the \emph{bound}, not the
problem: its values are all $\tfrac12$ and it is decided by inspection. What
it shows is that a coarse operator built by aggregating controlled vertices
cannot capture a slow mode that runs around a cycle longer than a block.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Aggregation that touches a controlled vertex is the
whole problem]\label{prop:prec-onectrl}
Suppose there is a polynomial-time algorithm which, given a stopping SSG $G$
and a designated $v\in C$, outputs a stochastic game $G'$ on
$V\setminus\{v\}$ with $\val_{G'}=\val_G$ off $v$. Then \textsc{SSG-Value}
is decidable in polynomial time.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
A controlled vertex of a stopping game has no self-loop (a self-loop is a
trap), so $v^{(0)},v^{(1)}\ne v$ and
$\val_G(v)=\max_i\val_G(v^{(i)})$ at $v\in\Vmax$, $\min$ at $v\in\Vmin$;
the outputs of the algorithm therefore name an optimal successor at $v$.
That is a sound decision rule in the sense of \Cref{def:decision-rule}, and
it is non-stalling because $v$ is arbitrary; \Cref{thm:decide-one-bit}
applies.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The general question}

\begin{theorem}[Preconditioning in general is
target-equivalent]\label{thm:prec-target}
The following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item \textsc{SSG-Value} is decidable in polynomial time.
\item There are polynomials $p,q$ and an algorithm which, given a stopping
      SSG $G$, outputs in time $p(|G|)$ a description of a monotone map
      $F:[0,1]^{V'}\to[0,1]^{V'}$, evaluable in time $p(|G|)$ on rationals
      of polynomial bit size, such that $F(\val)=\val$ and
      $\|F^{k}(\bbone)-F^{k}(0)\|_\infty\le(1-1/q(N))^{k}$ for all $k$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(a)$\Rightarrow$(b): take $F$ the constant map $\val$, computable by
hypothesis; it is monotone, fixes $\val$, and its bracket is $0$ after one
step. (b)$\Rightarrow$(a): $F$ monotone with $F(\val)=\val$ gives
$F^{k}(0)\le\val\le F^{k}(\bbone)$, and the width falls below $4^{-a}$ after
$O(q(N)\,a)$ steps; round each iterate outward to a multiple of
$2^{-p}$ with $p=\Theta(a+\log q(N))$ to keep the bit size bounded, and
recover $\val$ from the midpoint by continued fractions as in
\Cref{thm:prec-contract-class}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:prec-summary}
The three statements together delimit the route exactly. A change of
\emph{coordinates} that respects the order --- which by
\Cref{lem:prec-monomial} means a gauge --- cannot change the rate at all
(\Cref{thm:prec-invariance}), and the rate it cannot change is the largest
spectral radius among the $2^{|C|}$ profile chains
(\Cref{thm:prec-rate}), which is $1-2^{-\Theta(N)}$ already on the
player-free family $G_m$. A change of \emph{operator} does change the rate,
and the profile-independent part of the game --- the average vertices ---
can be contracted away once and for all, which strictly enlarges the escape
class (\Cref{thm:prec-contract-class,prop:prec-YD}) and in particular
absorbs $G_m$, where the class of \Cref{thm:escape-class} is empty of
content and value iteration is exponential by \Cref{thm:vi-lower}. Beyond
that, aggregation buys a factor equal to the block size for a cost
exponential in it (\Cref{prop:prec-block}), touching one controlled vertex
exactly is the whole problem (\Cref{prop:prec-onectrl}), and the
unrestricted question is the target (\Cref{thm:prec-target}).

Two further observations, both measured exactly. First, $\Lambda$ is not
merely a bound on the certificate: on $G_5,G_7$ and on $WD(4,2,6)$,
$WD(7,2,6)$ the observed per-round factor of the true two-sided bracket
$\|T^{k}\bbone-T^{k}0\|_\infty$ at $k=120$ agrees with $\Lambda$ to nine
decimal places ($0.963780988$, $0.991791422$, $0.976750819$,
$0.997342154$). But it is not always the bracket's rate: on $Y_D$ it is a
little below $\Lambda$ ($0.985530$ against $0.988904$ at $D=5$), and on
$Z_D$ the bracket contracts by exactly $\tfrac12$ per round while
$\Lambda=2^{-1/2}$, because there Min actively closes it. So the escape
certificate is sound and, by \Cref{thm:prec-rate}, optimal among
certificates, yet still not tight for value iteration itself; a tighter
certificate would have to read Min as a minimiser, which is exactly what
\Cref{lem:survival}(a) cannot afford. Second, $Y_D$ is not a stall: the
own-successor test of \Cref{rem:own-successor} for \Cref{def:slack}, seeded
with the free $Z_0,Z_1$ bounds and read in both directions, fires on $Y_D$
at rounds $8,11,14,17,20$ for $D=3,\dots,7$ --- linear, not exponential. A
long survival time is not by itself a difficulty; $G_m$, with no players at
all and $1-\Lambda=2^{-\Theta(N)}$, is solved by one linear solve.
\end{remark}
